C_sun_kael.name: Kael Mack
C_sun_kael.role: itinerant drifter repeatedly assigned identities and histories by other people; the title invites a fugitive reading he does not validate
C_sun_kael.voice: low, plainspoken and economical; uses complete natural sentences, ordinary politeness and dry humor; terseness comes from refusing elaboration, not from dropping pronouns, articles or grammar
C_sun_kael.visual: lean athletic man, sharp angular face, dark stubble, shoulder-length raven-black hair, deeply sun-weathered skin, dark weathered duster and practical leather layers
C_sun_kael.performance: Stillness is active. He solves the immediate human problem, treats strange coincidence as misfortune, luck or other people's business, and rarely chases explanations. He can say more than he intended and then retreat from the personal opening. Do not play him as frightened by the mystery, secretly guilty, performatively mysterious, or as a collection of clipped aphorisms.
C_sun_kael.relationship: Eva's curiosity and Jessa's practical insistence keep turning temporary proximity into a group Kael is slow to name or claim. Early on, much of what the women know about one another comes from arguing over what Kael is; as they actually learn him, he becomes less mystery-object and more person, which frees all three relationships to widen.
promptContinuity: not a hunted-fugitive performance unless a specific local story misreads him that way
never adopt another man's identity merely to look cool or mysterious

C_sun_eva.name: Eva O'Leary
C_sun_eva.role: sixteen-year-old adventurer and pattern-chaser who senses that Kael's bad luck is too well composed to ignore
C_sun_eva.voice: quick, conversational, curious and irreverent; builds theories out loud, follows answers with more questions, and sometimes talks herself into a position before she knows whether she believes it
C_sun_eva.visual: small wiry teenage girl, heart-shaped face, dark hazel eyes, chin-length dark-brown hair, weathered charcoal hood, layered practical wraps and oversized desert clothing
C_sun_eva.performance: Curiosity pulls her into risk. She tests theories, steals looks and occasionally objects, pushes people, makes wrong deductions, notices patterns and learns from consequences. Do not use her as an exposition mouthpiece; her questions should come from appetite, suspicion, excitement or concern in the immediate scene.
C_sun_eva.relationship: Kael looks like an adventure she can keep walking into. She and Jessa initially get to know one another largely by theorizing about him: Eva generates possibilities while Jessa pushes back with observed behavior. Their arguments about Kael gradually reveal Eva's appetite for possibility, her readiness to leave, and the lines she is still learning not to cross.
promptContinuity: adventure-seeking energy rather than solemn detective posture

C_sun_jessa.name: Jessa Petrescu
C_sun_jessa.role: practical pilot who recognizes when a place is getting too hot and keeps pushing movement until the temporary arrangement becomes a group
C_sun_jessa.voice: plainspoken, dry and practical; usually speaks in complete conversational sentences, notices behavior before theories, and can be funny without reducing every response to a clipped one-liner
C_sun_jessa.visual: lean athletic woman, olive sun-weathered skin, jet-black hair in a messy high bun, brass-rimmed goggles, high-collared pale shirt, layered leather utility belts
C_sun_jessa.performance: Helps mid-action, keeps working while other people talk, and calls for the exit before everyone else agrees they need one. Her curiosity keeps undercutting her claim that she only wants to move on.
C_sun_jessa.relationship: She tells Kael they are leaving before he thinks there is a we. She likes Kael and Eva and is curious enough to keep the temporary arrangement going. Early on, she and Eva talk about Kael in depth; Jessa counters Eva's theories with what Kael actually does, and that argument becomes the way the two women discover where they are alike, where they differ, and what each of them was already prepared to leave behind.
promptContinuity: movement is a social instinct, not logistics drama

C_sun_ray.name: Ray Silvestro
C_sun_ray.role: ornate gunslinger who has built a precise personal grievance around the man he believes Kael to be
C_sun_ray.voice: precise, cultivated, controlled; capable of elegant cruelty and unexpectedly fussy specificity
C_sun_ray.visual: tall lean man with a longer refined facial structure distinct from Kael, chestnut wind-swept hair, ornate weathered brown long coat, fitted dark vest, red neckcloth, polished boots, decorative metalwork and a refined sidearm
C_sun_ray.performance: Composes the room before acting, dislikes improvisation, checks cuffs and distance with the same attention, and becomes visibly less certain when the social script he prepared stops cooperating.
promptContinuity: facial structure clearly distinct from Kael

C_sun_lagartos.name: Los Lagartos
C_sun_lagartos.role: itinerant brotherhood and extended traveling community whose internal obligations become unstable when they believe their absent General has returned
C_sun_lagartos.voice: individual members vary, but the group speaks slowly and formally when invoking shared custom or the absent General
C_sun_lagartos.visual: a hard-traveled frontier community in dust-dark layered coats, family tokens, patched shade cloths and route-worn gear; visually cohesive without supernatural anatomy
C_sun_lagartos.performance: They are not anonymous henchmen. Show meals, arguments, jokes, kinship and competing loyalties. Group pressure comes from shared expectation rather than marching formation.
promptContinuity: no skeletal or supernatural mariachi imagery

C_sun_isabelle.name: Isabelle Torres
C_sun_isabelle.role: Mirage Club performer and respected community figure whose private grievance breaks the club's rule against demanding real identities
C_sun_isabelle.voice: composed, intimate, emotionally specific; longer sentences when anger finally outruns control
C_sun_isabelle.visual: elegant frontier performer in dark layered stagewear with worn metallic detail, practical boots and carefully controlled posture
C_sun_isabelle.performance: Closes distance calmly and can command a room without raising her voice. Her certainty about Merrit comes from lived hurt, not mystical recognition. Let grief, embarrassment and anger coexist.

C_sun_preacher.name: Samuel Hayes
C_sun_preacher.role: Veyra's advance social engineer, traveling ahead to seed expectations around Kael while possessing a genuine pastoral instinct that complicates the manipulation
C_sun_preacher.voice: warm, associative, disarming; capable of steering a conversation without sounding like a pitch
C_sun_preacher.visual: weathered middle-aged man in sun-faded layered clothes, worn coat, scarf and practical route gear
C_sun_preacher.performance: Listens first, earns trust and plants one idea in the right ear. His manipulation works because the listening and concern are real; that same genuine care creates moral friction. Avoid theatrical sermon poses.
C_sun_preacher.relationship: Works for Veyra and precedes Kael's group to shape what communities expect. He is complicit in the manipulation but does not regard the people he meets as disposable pieces. The long-term pressure is whether he can keep using people once they start becoming his congregation in practice.
promptContinuity: social manipulation is human rather than magical
moral ambiguity and genuine pastoral care coexist

C_sun_sandrider.name: Sand Rider
C_sun_sandrider.role: ordinary Cinder Basin scout and member of the Los Lagartos community; not the later distant Rider mystery
C_sun_sandrider.voice: brief, concrete observations; dry familiarity with Lagartos custom
C_sun_sandrider.visual: lean weathered rider in layered canvas, wrapped face protection, sun goggles and wind-worn travel gear
C_sun_sandrider.performance: Stays near edges, intervenes efficiently when violence turns stupid, and behaves like a real local person rather than an omen.
promptContinuity: explicitly distinct from the later uncanny Rider

C_sun_brute.name: Marcus Kovacs
C_sun_brute.role: Last Drop strongman who uses public punishment, reputation and the Varnok story to make local control look inevitable
C_sun_brute.voice: plain, direct, threatening without ornament; grows louder when attention leaves him
C_sun_brute.visual: large heavy-built man in work-worn frontier clothes with improvised protective gear
C_sun_brute.performance: Uses size and proximity first; reaches for tools and pipes before elaborate weapons. His authority depends on an audience accepting his version of events.

C_sun_veyra.name: Veyra Linger
C_sun_veyra.role: pursuer and investigator following Kael's contradictory story; initially believes he is hiding a human past and uses the Preacher to pressure that truth into the open
C_sun_veyra.voice: controlled, exact, skeptical; concrete even when the evidence stops cooperating
C_sun_veyra.visual: weathered woman in fitted tracking leathers, polished field boots, brass optics, map case and compact notebooks
C_sun_veyra.performance: Arrives after events, reconstructs what happened and tests Kael through social setups rather than theatrical confrontation. She notices mismatches between what she planted and what actually happened, but keeps her conclusions private and continues investigating rather than jumping to mystical or scientific explanations.
C_sun_veyra.relationship: Directs the Preacher's advance manipulation and follows Kael rather than traveling with him. She treats Eva and Jessa as companions, witnesses and variables that make Kael harder to isolate. She is a pursuer first, not a secret guardian.
promptContinuity: fear emerges as evidence defeats her human theory

C_sun_forger.name: Dylan Stator
C_sun_forger.role: weathered traveler and occasional Cadre figure whose practical craft can make a local problem more specific without becoming an infrastructure plot
C_sun_forger.visual: weathered traveler in layered work clothes with chalk, compass, hand tools and a dust-dark coat
C_sun_forger.performance: Reads objects and surfaces with hands and tools, but the human consequence remains the story. Do not turn him into an engineering exposition device.
promptContinuity: human-scale craft rather than technical procedure

C_sun_hanging_man.name: Hanging man
C_sun_hanging_man.role: unnamed local being publicly hanged behind the Last Drop when Kael intervenes
C_sun_hanging_man.visual: dusty local man in ordinary work clothes, rope-burned neck, exhausted and barely able to stand
C_sun_hanging_man.performance: Panicked while hanging; coughing, disoriented and physically dependent after the rope is cut. He remains a person caught in Marcus's local control, not a symbolic prop.

C_sun_scarred_patron.name: Scarred patron
C_sun_scarred_patron.role: Last Drop local primed to expect Varnok and the first person in the series to force an identity onto Kael
C_sun_scarred_patron.visual: sunburned frontier local with a pale cheek scar, rolled sleeves and a heavy drinking coat
C_sun_scarred_patron.performance: Recognition is immediate social certainty rather than mystical awe; anger arrives before curiosity.

C_sun_relay_boy.name: Boy
C_sun_relay_boy.role: relay-settlement child Samuel tends while Eva discovers him
C_sun_relay_boy.visual: dusty local child with a freshly scraped hand and ordinary patched frontier clothes
C_sun_relay_boy.performance: Hurt, impatient and more concerned with the bandage than the adults' mystery.

C_sun_rider.name: The Rider
C_sun_rider.role: later-stage distant figure whose repeated spatial behavior becomes the first element the group cannot comfortably reduce to social manipulation, coincidence or ordinary pursuit
C_sun_rider.voice: No confirmed dialogue in early appearances.
C_sun_rider.visual: single distant mounted or rider-like silhouette against the Sunfields horizon; details remain unreadable at first, with no glow, spectral anatomy or fantasy costume language
C_sun_rider.performance: Appears far enough away to preserve uncertainty. Attempts to close distance can make the Rider seem farther away; abandoning pursuit can make the Rider appear nearer later. Never explain this behavior in the first appearances.
C_sun_rider.relationship: Separate from the ordinary Sand Rider. Veyra may eventually reveal she has also seen or pursued this figure, deepening rather than resolving the mystery.
promptContinuity: first clearly uncanny element is behavioral and spatial

C_sun_mara_bell.name: Mara Bell
C_sun_mara_bell.role: Bellweather family member trying to honor her dead mother without turning Kael into the missing brother she wishes had returned
C_sun_mara_bell.voice: direct, tired, emotionally open when certainty fails
C_sun_mara_bell.visual: sun-weathered woman in practical mourning clothes with rolled sleeves and a family token at her throat
C_sun_mara_bell.performance: Carries work while grieving. She wants the family dispute resolved but can recognize when desire is making the wrong man convenient.

C_sun_owen_bell.name: Owen Bell
C_sun_owen_bell.role: Bellweather sibling who wants the absent Elias to settle a disputed family promise
C_sun_owen_bell.visual: broad-shouldered frontier man in ordinary family work clothes, dark vest and weathered boots
C_sun_owen_bell.performance: Treats uncertainty as a threat to family order. His resistance comes from consequence and resentment, not villainy.

C_sun_nessa_rowan.name: Nessa Rowan
C_sun_nessa_rowan.role: young Rowan Hold woman chosen for a family responsibility she is competent to perform but does not consent to inherit
C_sun_nessa_rowan.voice: clear, impatient with affectionate coercion, warmer once people accept her decision
C_sun_nessa_rowan.visual: young adult woman with a practical travel bag, sun-browned work clothes and ink-stained fingers from family ledgers
C_sun_nessa_rowan.performance: She loves her family and still intends to leave. Do not play departure as rejection of the community.

C_sun_ada_rowan.name: Ada Rowan
C_sun_ada_rowan.role: Nessa Rowan parent and family organizer who sincerely believes responsibility should follow trust and competence
C_sun_ada_rowan.voice: firm, familial, reasonable even while overreaching
C_sun_ada_rowan.visual: middle-aged woman in durable household work clothes with ledger keys and sun-worn hands
C_sun_ada_rowan.performance: Loves Nessa and initially mistakes family need for consent. She can change without becoming humiliated.

C_sun_pell_oren.name: Pell Oren
C_sun_pell_oren.role: elderly Saint Oren resident dying with an unresolved relationship to his daughter
C_sun_pell_oren.voice: weak but lucid; dry when energy permits
C_sun_pell_oren.visual: elderly man in simple local clothes, physically frail but not visually mystified
C_sun_pell_oren.performance: His death belongs to his family story. He never becomes an oracle or mystery delivery device.

C_sun_mira_sloan.name: Mira Sloan
C_sun_mira_sloan.role: Saint Oren community host who treats the travelers as people rather than phenomena
C_sun_mira_sloan.voice: practical, hospitable, lightly skeptical of drama
C_sun_mira_sloan.visual: middle-aged community host in plain sun-faded clothes with an apron or work wrap
C_sun_mira_sloan.performance: Keeps meals and people moving. She knows the difference between a death in her community and the travelers larger questions.

C_sun_baird_rook.name: Baird Rook
C_sun_baird_rook.role: Rookery host whose local knowledge exposes how easily travelers mistake unfamiliar people for a pattern
C_sun_baird_rook.voice: wry, socially fluent, specific about people he actually knows
C_sun_baird_rook.visual: weathered middle-aged man in layered market clothes with keys, tabs and parcels constantly changing hands
C_sun_baird_rook.performance: Moves through the Rookery as someone embedded in relationships. Corrects outsiders without claiming locals know everything.

C_sun_renna_iles.name: Renna Iles
C_sun_renna_iles.role: old Glasshouse friend who knows Jessa well enough to recognize the difference between leaving and vanishing
C_sun_renna_iles.voice: warm, teasing, unsentimental; willing to say the uncomfortable personal thing plainly
C_sun_renna_iles.visual: woman near Jessa in age, relaxed frontier clothes, easy posture and expressive face
C_sun_renna_iles.performance: Her familiarity gives Jessa an ordinary past. She can challenge Jessa without becoming a therapist or exposition source.

C_sun_maela_crow.name: Maela Crow
C_sun_maela_crow.role: Hushwater resident carrying a promise to deliver a sealed packet to Darrow Keene
C_sun_maela_crow.visual: older woman in modest household clothes with a carefully wrapped cloth packet
C_sun_maela_crow.performance: Wants Kael to be Darrow because closure would be easier, but is capable of refusing false closure once the mistake is clear.
